### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/rest`, touching **73** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**57** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4bba8b8f02fdbdf30e9ad41fc5d2a6fdd3ccaf2a`.

⛔ **18** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `environmentId (44 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 58 pages)`
- **18** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4bba8b8f02fdbdf30e9ad41fc5d2a6fdd3ccaf2a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e5d8edd608d9bdfe5221b0eafc4aeee334e5e6df` — the merge of head `be4a48ae3044fd52058048c8508b3d5fc877c57c` into base `4bba8b8f02fdbdf30e9ad41fc5d2a6fdd3ccaf2a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e5d8edd608d9bdfe5221b0eafc4aeee334e5e6df && git checkout e5d8edd608d9bdfe5221b0eafc4aeee334e5e6df
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4bba8b8f02fdbdf30e9ad41fc5d2a6fdd3ccaf2a be4a48ae3044fd52058048c8508b3d5fc877c57c && git checkout -B drift-repro 4bba8b8f02fdbdf30e9ad41fc5d2a6fdd3ccaf2a && git merge --no-ff be4a48ae3044fd52058048c8508b3d5fc877c57c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4bba8b8f02fdbdf30e9ad41fc5d2a6fdd3ccaf2a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4bba8b8f02fdbdf30e9ad41fc5d2a6fdd3ccaf2a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `1f741879a98e944a648aad37e953a2c9674dbffc`
Local-runs: none

The PR's own commits (`4cdb3b2d…1f741879`, on top of `e3f0cfd4`) were read. The rest of the range against today's main is main.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Your question: "inline definitions are not audited" is scope, not a narrowing arm.** Before this PR no dataset query wrote a row. After it, an opted-in saved-dataset query writes one, and every door answers exactly as before. Nothing a caller could send or read before is refused or reshaped. Clause-② item 5 asks about the accept set and the public surface, and leaving the inline path out shrinks neither. The widening declaration is right: a new `action` value, a new plugin option, a new `recordDatasetQuery` slot member, new exports, and two optional parameters on `createReadAuditBatcher` whose defaults keep the old behaviour.
- **The event boundary is right.**
  - `runAuditedDatasetQuery` wraps only `svc.queryDataset`, so every earlier refusal returns before it and hands no event: identity, body, selection, resolution, the holder judgment and the parse. The pins measure this.
  - A thrown read hands one `failed` event with `resolveThrownHttpError`'s status and code, never the message, and is rethrown unchanged.
  - The batch door goes through the same `answerDatasetQuery`, so each entry gets one event (pinned).
  - The sink is resolved per request, and its promise is not awaited, so the write stays off the request path. A throwing sink never changes the answer (pinned).
- **The row is right.** The principal, tenant, actor (presence-probed) and impersonation follow the CRUD mirror's rules. `metadata` keeps the dataset, dimension, measure and time-dimension names (bounded at 32 each, through `recordedField`), the filter as `summarizeExportFilter` terms with no comparands (pinned), `row_count`, `outcome`, and on a failure `status`/`error_code`. The row is stamped with the query instant (pinned) and written with `preserveAudit`. The writer is null when nothing is opted in, so nothing is buffered by default (pinned). Lost batches are reported at `error` once per cause, and overflow is reported once.
- **must-fix M1: the row does not say WHICH dataset when two packages hold the name.**
  - *Two holders are real.* `dataset` is a type stored per `(package, name)`. This door resolves `?package=`, `?callerPackage=` and the bare name per ADR-0150 D3, and since #33491 a contended name can be answered by one holder judged on its own item (`admitRefusedDatasetHolders`).
  - *The row loses the holder.* The event carries only `datasetName` and the dataset's `object`. The opt-in is keyed on the bare name, so an opted-in name audits every holder's queries under one indistinguishable `dataset` value, and an auditor cannot tell package A's dataset from package B's.
  - *The fix.* Pass the resolved holder from the item the door read (`read.item`'s package stamp, or `null` for the environment's own) into the event, and record it in `metadata` (for example `dataset_package`). Say in the option's doc and in record-view-auditing.mdx that a name in `datasets` covers every holder of that name. Add one pin at the rest layer: two holders of one name, a query at `?package=A` and one at `?package=B`, two rows that differ in `dataset_package`.
- **nit N1.** `previewDrafts` reads a draft definition under the same name. If the door knows it served a draft, recording `preview: true` would keep a draft read distinguishable from a published one. Optional.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-audit: patch` and `@objectstack/rest: patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. That is correct for a non-protocol widening. M1 adds a metadata key to a new row, which stays inside this widening.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Tenant audit census 314 → 315 and the durability-registry entry are regenerated with the new insert site. The enum ledger and the label pins cover the new action value.
- CI at this head: no failing checks. One Check Changeset run was cancelled by a newer run. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.
- No file conflict with #33491 or #33512 (per the area).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `be4a48ae3044fd52058048c8508b3d5fc877c57c`
Local-runs: none

This reviews the delta on my FAIL at `1f741879a98e944a648aad37e953a2c9674dbffc`. The PR-side commits are `9a177815` (red pins), `37cead9a` (fix) and `99e4217b` (pin order). After them come a merge of main (`c1014aa8`) and a census re-measure (`be4a48ae`).

### ① Derived judgments

- **M1 closed.**
  - *The door.* It now keeps the item the by-name read served (`served = read?.item`, captured before translation and strip) and hands `datasetPackage: holderPackageOf(served)`. That is the item's `_packageId`, or `null` for the environment's own definition (`sys_metadata` or unstamped).
  - *The row.* The writer records it as `metadata.dataset_package`, bounded to a package-id shape (`?` otherwise).
  - *The pin.* A rest pin holds two holders of `sales`. It queries `?package=com.acme.crm` and `?package=com.acme.ops` and gets two events that differ in `datasetPackage`. A plugin-audit pin orders the two rows by row count.
  - *The docs.* The option doc, the changeset and record-view-auditing.mdx say that a name covers every holder and that each row names the holder it read.
- **N1 taken.** A served draft (`_draft`) records `preview: true` (pinned together with the environment's own definition recording `dataset_package: null`).
- **Merge and census.** The merge brings in main. The census re-measure on the merged main changes only the counts doc and the census mdx. No PR-side source changed in either commit.
- **Note.** The holder is read from the served item's `_packageId` stamp, the same marker other doors read a holder from. An item served unstamped would be recorded as the environment's (`null`). This is consistent with how the metadata read serves package items today.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and correct: `@objectstack/plugin-audit: patch`, `@objectstack/rest: patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The two new metadata keys sit inside the new row.

### ③ Boundary flags

The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.
